payload.title: Scheduling: publish a chosen version at a chosen time (backend)
payload.description:
Part of the scheduled publishing and announcements epic. Design: docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md ("Scheduling model").

Goal: an editor pins one version of a Story to a UTC moment; at that moment the normal publish path publishes it exactly once, unless a newer version was saved after scheduling.

Shape: fields `scheduledPublishAt`, `scheduledBy`, `scheduledAt`, `scheduleState` (sparse: only `scheduled`/`publishing`/`blocked`), `scheduleName` on the version's Item row; one new Item index `scheduleState+scheduledPublishAt` (the only index in that deploy); EventBridge Scheduler `papyrus-pub-<siteId>-<item8>` (`at()`, UTC, ActionAfterCompletion DELETE) invoking content-actions `publish-scheduled` through a scheduler role limited to that prefix, with retries and a dead-letter queue with an alarm; conditional claim before publishing; schedule removed on success, on publish-now and on retire. Settings: `publication.timeZone` (IANA) required when scheduling is on.

Depends on: PPY-271940 (first publication time carried forward). Deploy: schema fields + one index; plugin/IaC for the scheduler role and DLQ.

```gherkin
Feature: A Story goes live at the time an editor chose
  Our newsroom writes faster than we want to publish, so an editor picks when each
  Story goes out and the system publishes it then, without anyone at a keyboard.

  Background:
    Given the publication's time zone is America/New_York
    And Sam may publish on this site

  Scenario: A scheduled version is published at its time
    Given Sam scheduled version 3 of "Robots in the warehouse" for 13 November 2026 at 09:00 New York time
    When 13 November 2026 at 14:00 UTC arrives
    Then version 3 is published
    And the Story's published time is the moment it went live
    And the version records that it was published as scheduled by Sam
    And the Story no longer shows a schedule

  Scenario: A newer version saved after scheduling is not published by surprise
    Given Sam scheduled version 3 for 13 November at 09:00
    And the copywriting agent saved version 4 on 12 November
    When 13 November at 09:00 arrives
    Then nothing is published
    And the schedule says "A newer version was saved after this was scheduled. Schedule it again."
    And the site's editors are told

  Scenario: The same schedule firing twice publishes once
    Given a scheduled version whose schedule fires twice at the same moment
    When both runs try to publish it
    Then it is published once
    And the second run stops without changing anything

  Scenario: A stale schedule does not publish after a change of time
    Given Sam moved a schedule from 09:00 to 11:00
    When a run for 09:00 arrives late
    Then nothing is published at that run
    And the version is still scheduled for 11:00

  Scenario: Publishing now ends the schedule
    Given version 3 is scheduled for tomorrow
    When Sam publishes version 3 now
    Then it is published now
    And the schedule is removed and will not fire

  Scenario: Retiring a Story removes its schedule
    Given a Story with a scheduled version
    When an editor retires the Story
    Then its schedule is removed

  Scenario: A scheduled new version keeps the first publication date
    Given a Story first published on 4 November
    And its version 5 is scheduled for 14 November at 08:00
    When version 5 is published on schedule
    Then the Story's published time is still 4 November
    And the served version's published time is 14 November at 08:00

  Scenario: A missed schedule is visible, not silently handled
    Given a schedule that failed every retry
    Then an alarm reaches the operators
    And the newsroom shows the Story as "Overdue" with its scheduled time

  Scenario: A time that does not exist is refused
    When Sam asks to schedule for 8 March 2026 at 02:30 New York time
    Then the request is refused with "That time does not exist on 8 March in New York. Pick another time."

  Scenario: A time that happens twice must be chosen
    When Sam asks to schedule for 1 November 2026 at 01:30 New York time
    Then Sam is asked to choose between 01:30 EDT and 01:30 EST

  Scenario: Only people who may publish may schedule
    Given Lee may edit but not publish
    When Lee tries to schedule a version
    Then the request is refused with "You can't publish on this site, so you can't schedule."
```

Open questions: none blocking; the editors' notice for a blocked schedule uses the Caducus operator-class kind until reader audiences exist.
